library_preparation_preflight.summary: Base org.bytedeco:ffmpeg artifact ships no native binaries; needs the ffmpeg-platform aggregator at test runtime, matching the convention already used by every other org.bytedeco library in this repo (tesseract, openblas, flycapture, libdc1394, librealsense2).

deterministic_setup.reason: org.bytedeco:ffmpeg contains only Java wrapper classes; ffmpeg-platform is the aggregator that pulls in the per-OS/arch native shared libraries (avcodec, avformat, avutil, swscale, swresample, etc.) required for any native call to succeed under both the JVM agent run and native-image.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: The published org.bytedeco:ffmpeg-platform build is the LGPL variant: it excludes GPL-only codecs such as libx264/libx265. Write tests against FFmpeg's built-in/LGPL-safe codecs and containers (e.g. mpeg4, png, software scaling via swscale, resampling via swresample) rather than requiring H.264/H.265 encoding — pulling in org.bytedeco:ffmpeg-platform-gpl or the org.bytedeco.javacpp.platform.extension=-gpl system property would add GPL-licensed native code to the dependency tree and is a licensing decision outside scaffold generation, not something to default to. Expect the platform aggregator to download native binaries for every supported OS/arch (it has no variant-aware filtering here, consistent with how other bytedeco modules in this repo already behave) — this is a materially larger download than typical libraries but not blocking.
risks: ffmpeg-platform pulls native binaries for all listed platforms (android-arm64/x86_64, linux-x86_64/arm64, macosx-arm64/x86_64, windows-x86_64), which is a sizeable download compared to most libraries in this repo.
If generated tests end up needing a GPL-only codec, that's a legal/licensing decision for a human, not something to default into automatically.
